page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware configuration features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 20 physical cores and 20 vCPUs utilizing an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. System memory consists of 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high resource density of 12.8 GB per core. Graphics and parallel processing workloads are accelerated by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with the stress-ng single-core test and Geekbench single-core score both placing in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% across stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is consistently strong in the top 25% for both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes. In cryptographic and vector execution, the processor supports AVX-512 and VAES, contributing to strong performance in extended instruction sets. However, Ray Tracing and PassMark CPU encryption benchmarks fall into the average tier.

For specialized workloads, the NVIDIA L40S GPU delivers top-tier performance in small-model LLM inference, achieving 4434.62 tokens per second for prompt processing and 386.89 tokens per second for text generation with a 135M model. Medium-model text generation remains strong, while large-model inference falls to average speeds. This profile makes the server suitable for machine learning inference, image processing, and database operations. The primary architectural tradeoffs include the shared CPU allocation model and the complete absence of local storage, requiring external storage attachments for persistent data.
